key_insight: The paper shows that fair policies in multi-objective reinforcement learning can be learned as a diverse Pareto-optimal set, rather than a single solution tied to one fixed preference.
engineering_relevance: This enables decision systems to serve different users or changing priorities while preserving both performance and equity across competing objectives.
method: Prove fair solutions under concave piecewise-linear welfare functions lie in the convex coverage set (CCS).
Extend multi-policy MORL with generalized Gini welfare function (GGF) to learn fair policy sets.
Add state-augmented non-stationary and stochastic policy variants to adapt fairness to reward history and changing preferences.
evidence_signal: The methods were evaluated across multiple domains and compared with state-of-the-art MORL baselines, showing that the learned policy sets support different user preferences.
watch_item: The added non-stationary and stochastic policy machinery may increase implementation complexity and training instability compared with standard single-policy MORL.
paper_title: Learning Fair Pareto-Optimal Policies in Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning
